title: Address head-of-line blocking causing long-context tail latency across deployment modes
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary: Several customers (hosted and Dedicated enterprise) reported severe tail latency for requests that include very long contexts (~100k tokens). Symptoms included small interactive requests waiting behind a small number of long-context streaming generations, leading to 95th/99th percentile spikes and production escalations. This ticket tracks root-cause, bugfixes in the continuous batching scheduler, and coordinated rollouts across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Background: The serving runtime's continuous batching scheduler attempts to maximize GPU utilization by greedily assembling batches by arrival order. Long-context requests allocate large KV cache and take significantly longer to complete per token, which can cause head-of-line blocking when preemption is not enforced: small requests arriving after a long request are delayed until the large request yields. This reproduces as queue hogging and long-context tail latency regressions under mixed workloads.

Goal: Fix scheduler imbalance and introduce safeguards so that long-context generations do not materially increase interactive tail latency across deployment modes while preserving throughput and cost targets. Deliver a patch in runtime-1.19, coordinated canary and rollout plan, and verification dashboards and synthetic test suites.
comments: 2025-02-18 - Maya Patel: Created ticket after customer support escalations from two Hosted customers and one Dedicated pilot. Attached initial incident notes and Grafana slices. Linked PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RT/HOl-blocking-incident-2025-02

2025-02-19 - Diego Martinez: Reproduced locally with mixed synthetic workload (10% long-context:100k tokens, 90% short: <512 tokens) using runtime perf harness. Confirmed >3x increase in p99 for short requests when long requests present. Test harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-harness/tree/feature/mixed-long-context

2025-02-20 - Diego Martinez: Root cause hypothesis: scheduler's batch window and per-batch KV reservation allocate cache and CPU/GPU occupancy to long requests; missing preemption and lack of size-aware prioritization allows head-of-line blocking. Also observed suboptimal KV cache eviction policy that prevents small requests from reusing hot prefixes when long contexts monopolize memory.

2025-02-21 - Engineering triage meeting notes: Prioritize (1) small change to enforce per-request max-queue-time and size-aware prioritization, (2) implement cooperative preemption by splitting long-context requests into smaller token-commit chunks for scheduling, (3) KV cache eviction policy adjustments. Diego to prototype preemption; Maya to own rollout plan and customer communications.

2025-02-24 - Diego Martinez: Opened implementation branch implementing a priority queue with size buckets and per-request max_queue_ms. Work-in-progress PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1824. Prototype shows p99 reduction from 600ms->120ms for short requests in mixed-run on A100-80GB emulation.

2025-02-25 - Ben Liu (SRE): Verified Canary dashboards for preemption prototype under controlled traffic. Added Grafana panels: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/long-tail-dashboard. Observed minor throughput loss (~3%) but large tail improvements. SLO impact acceptable for P0 fix.

2025-02-26 - UX/PM (Ava Chen): Drafted customer-facing status update for Hosted customers and playbook for Dedicated support engineers to toggle new flags. Template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RT/LongContext-Communication

2025-02-27 - Code review feedback (L2): Asked to add unit tests for scheduler fairness and to add metrics for 'preempted_requests' and 'queue_reorders'. Diego updated PR with tests and metrics. PR now ready for CI: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1824#pullrequestreview-221
2025-02-28 - Security review (note): No secrets or customer data changes. KMS/HSM not impacted. Marked security_review_required = false. Sec reviewed the patch and raised no concerns.

2025-03-01 - Maya Patel: Plan for staged rollout: 10% canary Hosted (24h), then 50% (48h) if metrics stable, then full. Dedicated: feature-flagged control plane changelog; recommend administrators enable in non-peak window and run perf smoke tests. Private: publish upgrade notes and a config toggle; offer SE assistance for customers on air-gapped installs.

2025-03-01 - Diego Martinez: Next steps: merge PR after green CI, trigger canary rollout, add synthetic mixed-workload job to production Canary cluster for 72h, and monitor 'short_request_p99' and 'preempted_requests' metrics. Postmortem write-up to be added after rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Short-request p95/p99 latency returns to baseline under mixed workload (<=1.2x baseline p99) on Hosted canary
Throughput degradation <=5% for representative long-context-heavy workloads
New metrics exposed: scheduler.queue_time_ms, scheduler.preempted_requests, scheduler.queue_reorders
Canary rollout completed and no critical regressions observed for 72h
Documentation updated: Dedicated/Private config flags and upgrade notes published
